equation_request.abstract: In this work we address two questions concerning Grover’s algorithm. In the first we give an answer to the question how to employ Grover’s algorithm for actual search over database. We introduce a quantum model of an unordered phone book (quantum database) with programmable queries to search in the phone book either for a number, or for a name. In the second part we investigate how successful the algorithm can be if the number of elements of the database is not known precisely. This question reduces to analysis of the distinguishability of states occurring during Grover’s algorithm. We found that using unambiguous discrimination scheme even a seemingly good guess, that is close to the optimal one can result in a rather small success rate.

specification.problem: Grover search over a small quantum phone book (find index whose number or name equals a programmable query), plus analysis of unambiguous discrimination between Grover states produced for two different database sizes N and N' after the same t iterations.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Tiny instance: N=4 (k=2 index qubits), M=1, 2-bit names and 2-bit numbers stored by controlled-X gates, one number query; then overlap and IDP success computed from statevectors for two sizes (e.g. N=4 vs N'=8) with the same t. Excluded: general programmable-query database model details of the paper, M>1, multi-entry priors, exact unknown-size parametrization, optimal/non-IDP discrimination.

symbols.meaning: Grover angle for true size N
Grover angle for alternative size N'
query value held in query register
unambiguous discrimination success probability with equal priors

equations.label: Database state
equations.description: State after index Hadamards and loading of classical entries with controlled-X gates.
equations.justification: Sketch construction of the quantum phone book; the abstract only mentions a quantum database with programmable queries.

equations.label: Comparison oracle
equations.description: Phase-flip on entries matching the query; for a name search replace num by name.
equations.justification: Standard compare-by-CX plus multi-controlled-X onto a |-> ancilla; load and unload data registers around each use.
assumptions: Data registers are unloaded after the phase flip so only the index register is diffused

equations.label: Grover iteration count
equations.description: Near-optimal number of iterations for the known size.
equations.justification: Standard Grover analysis; for N=4, M=1 this gives t=1 and success probability 1.

equations.label: State after t steps
equations.description: Grover state in the 2D span of the good and bad subspaces.
equations.justification: Standard Grover geometry; the abstract only says the question reduces to distinguishability of states during Grover's algorithm.
assumptions: Same marked set in both runs

equations.label: Overlap
equations.description: Overlap of states for sizes N and N' with the same t, and the same good/bad basis.
equations.abstract_quote: This question reduces to analysis of the distinguishability of states occurring during Grover’s algorithm.
equations.justification: Follows from eq_4 when both states are written in a common good/bad basis; this requires identifying the two Hilbert spaces, which is an assumption.
assumptions: Identification of the good/bad basis across different N, N' (e.g. embed the smaller database)

equations.label: IDP success
equations.description: Ivanovic-Dieks-Peres unambiguous discrimination success probability for two pure states with equal priors.
equations.justification: Standard IDP bound; the abstract names unambiguous discrimination but gives no formula.

registers.name: index
registers.role: search index, in uniform superposition, diffused

registers.name: query
registers.role: classical query value; may be encoded by X gates on the comparison register instead of a separate register

specification.initial_state: All qubits |0>, then X and H on flag to make |->, H on index register.

steps.description: Prepare index uniform superposition and flag in |->.
Load name and number via controlled-X gates controlled on index values.
Apply comparison oracle for the chosen query (number or name register), then unload the data registers.
Apply diffusion on the index register (H, X, multi-controlled Z, X, H).
Repeat the oracle and diffusion steps t times.
For discrimination: build final index states for N and N' with the same t and compute overlap from statevectors, then the IDP success.

specification.measurement: Search: measure the index register only, then look up the name or number classically. Discrimination: no measurement, read the statevector.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Map measured index to the (name, number) table; compute |overlap| from statevector inner product and P_IDP=1-|overlap|.
assumptions: N power of two, small, M=1
Two candidate sizes with the same t
Entries are constants loaded by controlled-X
Ancilla compute/uncompute keeps qubits under the cap
missing_information: Paper's actual quantum database model and programmable query construction
How the unknown-size parametrization is defined
Exact states and priors used in the discrimination analysis
